description: Screenshot of an Urban Dictionary 'Top Definition' entry for the phrase 'paint the roses red', submitted by user DeTurk on December 3, 2008. The definition ties the phrase to frantically covering up a mistake with severe consequences and credits Alice in Wonderland for popularizing it. Standard Urban Dictionary layout with hashtags, vote counts (37 up / 10 down) and social share icons.
text: TOP DEFINITION. paint the roses red. To frantically attempt to cover up a mistake with severe consequences. Popularized by alice in wonderland. I accidently broke me mom's favorite antique vase so i had to paint the roses red. #cover up #fix #duct tape #clean #save. by DeTurk December 03, 2008. 37 10

description: Low-resolution photograph of a young Barack Obama wearing a white kufi-style cap and a dark embroidered traditional tunic, flanked by two unidentified women. The image is consistent with widely circulated photos reported to be from his half-brother Malik Obama's wedding in the early 1990s. Black letterbox bars on the sides indicate the image is a video frame grab or re-crop.
flags: The two women are unidentified private individuals
Wedding/date context is the commonly reported origin, not shown in the image itself
Image widely recirculated with political captions about Obama's religion

description: Scan of a vintage newspaper clipping by regional editor Arnie Hoffman about the 1979 Iran crisis, profiling Peter P. Strzok, 43, a former Gilman-area man who had left Iran on Feb. 6. Strzok, described as a Bell Helicopter Inc. support unit manager with prior military service in Iran, expresses hope that Ayatollah Khomeini's government will stabilize the country. A photo of a bespectacled man in a dark jacket is captioned 'Peter Strzok'. This is the father of FBI agent Peter Strzok; the clipping circulated in Q-related threads for that connection.
text: By Arnie Hoffman. Regional editor. America as a country is despised because it was seen as a supporter of the Shah of Iran, but individual Americans were treated well in respect to the crisis in Iran according to a former Gilman area man who left that Asian nation Feb. 6. Peter P. Strzok, 43, son of Mr. and Mrs. Mike Strzok, now living in Eau Claire, said he hopes the government of Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini will stabilize the country. 'I'd like very much to go back to Iran,' said Strzok, who spent two terms of military service and seven months as a civilian in the country. On the issue of treatment of Americans in Iran, Strzok, who was a support unit manager for Bell Helicopter Inc., said, the resentment of America was because Iranians [text cut off]. Peter Strzok
flags: Man pictured is Peter Strzok Sr. (father of the FBI agent), identified from the article text; the connection to the FBI agent is the sharer's implied claim
Bottom of the article is cut off mid-sentence

description: Line chart titled 'US Pneumonia Deaths - Weekly' plotting weekly pneumonia deaths by flu season (2013-14 through 2019-20) from CDC/NCHS mortality surveillance data, with source URLs cited at top. Each season is a colored line across week numbers 40-39; the red 2019-20 line ends with a sharp downward drop around week 11 (early 2020). Circulated during the early COVID-19 period, typically to suggest pneumonia deaths were falling or being reclassified; the drop at the line's end reflects incomplete recent-week reporting.

description: Black-and-white 'Spygate' meme: a photo montage places Barack Obama front and center with John Brennan, James Clapper, Andrew McCabe and James Comey arrayed behind him under the headline 'SPYGATE!'. The caption below claims Obama was the first ex-president to collude with others to impede the next sitting president. The image asserts, without evidence, the Spygate narrative of an Obama-directed conspiracy against Trump.
text: SPYGATE! Never has a president left office to collude with others to impede the next sitting president of the United States of America until Obama!
flags: The collusion claim is the meme's unverified assertion, presented here as a documented claim only
